coding.case_type: Patent: PTAB trials (IPR, PGR, CBM) and inter partes reexams

issues.description: Claim construction of 'caching': Board declined to limit caching to occur while rules are being swapped; affirmed construction favoring petitioner
issues.quote: We agree with Keysight and the Board. The claims already require caching to occur in response to the signaling and after "ceasing processing of one or more packets by the network protection device."

issues.description: Anticipation/substantial evidence that Hayter teaches caching entire data packets (limitation found in prior art)
issues.quote: Substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Hayter teaches caching entire data packets.

issues.description: Obviousness of claim 1 over Roese: Roese teaches preprocessing prior to implementation
issues.quote: We affirm the Board's conclusion of obviousness of claim 1.

issues.description: Obviousness of dependent claims 2, 15, and 19 (timing limitation for receipt of second rule set after implementation of first)
issues.quote: The Board's decision is supported by substantial evidence.

issues.description: APA notice challenge to Board's change in construction of 'being implemented' between institution and final decision; no violation found
issues.quote: We agree with the Board that there was no APA violation here because the Board's construction did not substantively change.

coding.author: Linn
coding.notes: Nonprecedential affirmance of IPR obviousness decision. Keysight's alternative collateral estoppel ground not reached and so not coded. Obviousness ruling for claim 1 is coded under P03 with ruling second (obvious). The X06 APA-notice issue was resolved on the merits of the notice argument, favoring the Board's decision; coded first (agency upheld) with favored side_b.

coding.side_a_parties: DS Advanced Enterprises, Ltd. (patent owner, appellant); Patrick Cummins (DS Advanced's counsel, sanctioned party)
coding.side_b_parties: Lowe's Home Centers, LLC (accused infringer, cross-appellant)

issues.description: Literal infringement: summary judgment of noninfringement of the metal housing limitation affirmed because the accused plastic housing and metal disc do not meet the construed metal housing limitation
issues.quote: Because no reasonable jury could find that the accused product has a metal housing, the district court correctly concluded that there is no genuine dispute of material fact as to infringement.

issues.description: Denial of motion to alter or amend the judgment under Rules 52(b) and 59(e)
issues.quote: Nor did the district court abuse its discretion by denying DS Advanced's motion to alter or amend the judgment.

issues.description: Discovery sanctions against counsel Cummins for violating the protective order, including finding of violation and sanction imposed
issues.quote: The district court did not err in finding a violation of the protective order.

issues.description: Rule 37(b)(2)(C) expense award against counsel (capped at 25,000 dollars) for violating the protective order
issues.quote: Nor did the district court abuse its discretion in setting the amount of sanctions.

issues.description: Denial of Lowe's motion for attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. 285 and sanctions under 28 U.S.C. 1927 on cross-appeal
issues.quote: We affirm the denial of the motion for fees and sanctions.

issues.description: Appellate jurisdiction over counsel's appeal of sanctions despite notice of appeal naming only DS Advanced; court found jurisdiction
issues.quote: Because the appeal unambiguously includes the sanctions orders, and the sanctions were imposed solely on Mr. Cummins, there is no confusion as to whether the client, the attorney, or both are appealing from the judgment. Thus, we have jurisdiction over Mr. Cummins' appeal.

coding.author: Stark
coding.notes: Nonprecedential disposition, affirmed in all respects; unanimous panel with no dissents. Cross-appeal by Lowe's on fees denial also affirmed. Claim construction of metal housing was not challenged, so no P11 issue coded. Lowe's motion for sanctions under FRAP 38 on the cross-appeal was denied in footnote 4 and is not coded as a separate issue.

coding.side_b_parties: Secretary of the Army (United States Army Corps of Engineers)

issues.description: Constructive change to the contract under the FAR 52.243-4 Changes Clause: whether Walsh plausibly pleaded a compensable constructive change entitling it to an equitable adjustment from the government's COVID-19 vaccine mandate actions, reversing the Board's dismissal.
issues.quote: Because Walsh's complaint sufficiently alleges a constructive change, we reverse and remand for further proceedings, including full analysis of the government's sovereign-acts-doctrine defense, which the Board did not address.

issues.description: Rule 12(b)(6) pleading sufficiency: whether the Board properly dismissed Walsh's complaint for failure to state a claim; the court held the complaint states a plausible claim.
issues.quote: We conclude that the Board took an impermissibly cramped view of the pleading in conducting the necessary inquiry into whether Walsh presented well-pleaded allegations of fact that, taken as true, state a plausible claim for relief under the constructive-change doctrine.

issues.description: Forfeiture: the government's argument that the constructive-change doctrine never applies to firm-fixed-price contracts was raised only in a footnote on appeal and held not preserved.
issues.quote: In this court, the government adverts to that position only in a footnote, Government Response Br. at 27 n.10, and so it has not adequately preserved the argument

coding.author: Taranto
coding.notes: Nonprecedential disposition from the ASBCA. The court declined to reach the government's sovereign acts defense, leaving it to the Board, so it is not coded as a decided issue. No dissent was noted.

coding.case_type: Federal employment (MSPB, arbitrator, OCWR, back-pay claims)

issues.description: Adverse action merits: Board's findings that the charged conduct occurred and that there was a nexus to the efficiency of the service, reviewed for substantial evidence.
issues.quote: What remains of Mr. Kroenung's appeal are challenges to the substantial evidence on which the Board relied in finding that the "charged conduct occurred," there is a "nexus between the conduct and the efficiency of the service."

issues.description: Penalty reasonableness under the Douglas factors: removal sustained, with no true comparators shown.
issues.quote: Mr. Kroenung has not satisfied this standard, particularly as he failed to identify any true comparator employees

issues.description: Forfeiture: grounds of illegality of the testing policy (executive overreach, enjoined executive order, EUA status, experimental nature of tests) not raised before DOD or the Board and therefore not reviewed.
issues.quote: The first four of these grounds of illegality were not presented to DOD and/or the Board and, hence, have been forfeited and are not before us.

issues.description: Forfeiture: challenge that the agency ignored the ninth and tenth points in the November 4, 2022 response, not raised at the Board.
issues.quote: Mr. Kroenung forfeited this challenge by not raising it at the Board.

issues.description: Jurisdiction: the court lacks jurisdiction to decide alleged ADA violations, which must be brought before the EEOC or a district court.
issues.quote: We lack jurisdiction to decide alleged violations of the ADA; these claims must be brought before the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission or a district court and cannot be asserted against the federal government.

issues.description: Trial and case management: AJ's exclusion of witness Brett Markham and denial of post-hearing briefing upheld as within discretion.
issues.quote: Mr. Kroenung falls far short of showing these case management decisions were an abuse of discretion.

coding.author: Stark
coding.notes: Nonprecedential affirmance of MSPB removal for refusing to comply with DOD COVID-19 testing policy. Court rejected the CDC-guidance illegality argument on the merits (policy not shown inconsistent with CDC guidance); I did not code that separately, as it is folded into the charge and penalty review. Motions for judicial notice and supplemental briefing were denied, not coded. No dissents.
